ядра.подтема: промпт/как Google пишет формат в примерах
ядра.ядро_en: In Google's example prompts the aspect ratio is commonly written inside the prompt text (e.g. '16:9 aspect ratio', 'Format 16:9', 'in 16:9 format', 'landscape 16:9'), usually at the end; DeepMind, blog and Think with Google pages show no separate parameter, while cookbook and Vertex samples may also set it by parameter.

модели_различия.текст_en: DeepMind Pro page, Pro blogs, Think with Google.
DeepMind NB2 page, NB2 blog, A2UI codelab, cookbook.
Vertex interleaved example page that lists Lite among its models (E-60-14); the cookbook turn example (E-20-38) runs with the notebook default model, which is not a model sign.
Vertex: interleaved example.

оговорки.текст_en: Wordings used by Google examples (verbatim): "16:9 aspect ratio"; "Format 16:9"; "Make the aspect ratio 16:9."; "The 16:9 poster is displayed on …"; "in 16:9 format"; "generate one at a time, 16:9 each"; "Each frame should be a landscape 16:9"; "Each image should be a separate output in 16:9 format."; "16:9, make 10 versions, one at a time"; "AR: 16:9"; "with 2:3 aspect ratio"; a bare "16:9" at the end; "generate each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio"; "square aspect ratio"; "in an ultra-wide panoramic shot".
For series, the format is stated per frame together with count and order ("10 frames, one by one", "Generate 6 images one at a time").
Think with Google (Asset Studio UI): aspect ratio is a prompt element and an edit prompt ("change aspect ratio"); no API parameter — not to be transferred to the API without checking.

Per-page observations: on the DeepMind Pro and NB2 pages, the Pro blogs and Think with Google no separate aspect-ratio parameter is shown next to the example prompts (extractor inference for each page).

Counter-examples: the cookbook turn example "Bring it back to the bedroom in an ultra-wide panoramic shot" runs with aspect_ratio 16:9 in the config, and the Vertex page with the interleaved example also shows REST imageConfig.aspectRatio "16:9".

словарь_терминов.значение_en: Aspect ratio of the output image; in the API a string such as "16:9" (an enum of 14 values), in prompts written as text ("16:9 aspect ratio", "Format 16:9"). Variant readings: the NB2 product page FAQ calls the ratio "size" (E-213-20); the Skills lab calls the resolution a "quality setting" (E-222-13).
Size (resolution) of the output image: 512, 1K, 2K, 4K; default 1K. Variant readings: "512" / "512px" / "0.5K" / "05.K" (a typo); for Lite the text says "1024px (1K)" (E-12-10).

Size classes; the label "1K (1024)" is the side of the square, for non-square formats the long side is larger (16:9 at 2K = 2752x1536). Variant readings: DeepMind writes lowercase "1k, 2k or 4k" (E-135-42), while a lowercase k is rejected in the parameter (E-1-78).

The smallest size (about 0.25 MP), for speed; available on NB2. Variant readings: a Vertex release note calls it "0.5MP" (a source typo, E-53-18); the cookbook and Firebase also attribute 512 to Lite (not accepted).
The image output token limit in the model card, not the 4K resolution. Variant readings: for 2.5 it is "32K token output" (E-170-4).

Object with image parameters inside generationConfig (generateContent: Vertex REST, SDK, Firebase). Variant readings: in the Interactions OpenAPI, ImageConfig / image_config is deprecated (E-41-7, E-41-8).
The new schema: an entry {"type": "image", aspect_ratio, image_size, mime_type, delivery}. Variant readings: the description of the response_format field mentions only a JSON schema (E-28-6).

The old form inside generation_config (removed after 2026-06-08); image_generation_config is the name used in the cookbook. Variant readings: the references do not use the name image_generation_config.
The format parameter in the OpenAI-compatible layer.

Tokenization resolution of INPUT media: low / medium / high / ultra_high (64 / 256 / 256 "zoomed reframing" tokens). Variant readings: ULTRA_HIGH exists at the Part level but not at the GenerationConfig level.
File format of the output image: only image/jpeg in response_format. Variant readings: Firebase says "always PNG" (E-228-26); Vertex uses imageOutputOptions.mimeType png (E-89-10).

In NB2 blogs, the name of the 2K/4K capability; on DeepMind pages, enlarging a finished image; in products, the 2K/4K dropdown or a Flow plan. Variant readings: the specifications call 2K/4K "built-in generation" (E-1-36).
A marketing phrase in blogs ("native support for 16:9, 9:16, 2:1, and more"). Variant readings: 2:1 from the same phrase is not in the specifications.
Cookbook labels for 1:4 / 4:1 and 1:8 / 8:1.
Groups of 2.5 aspect ratios in the developer blog; 5:4 and 4:5 are "Flexible". Variant readings: NotebookLM uses the orientations Square / Portrait / Landscape (E-256-9).
An empty image of the needed dimensions, passed before the text to set the shape of the result (2.5 recipe).
Extending an image beyond its original borders using a larger canvas.
In model cards: output at 1K (small text is often blurry).
Think with Google terms: one master concept turned into all formats; the "tax" of manual versions and resizing.
The Skills lab's name for the size (2K): "to control the detail and file size". Variant readings: in the same document the section is called "Image sizes".
Imagen 4 resolution parameter (1K / 2K, default 1K). Variant readings: in the SDK it is GenerateImagesConfig(image_size).
Imagen JPEG compression, 0 to 100, default 75. Variant readings: the direction of the scale is described ambiguously.
Feature status on Vertex: 4K was preview from 2026-05-28 and GA from 2026-08-31.
